label: copy-phase input k in short sequences
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the token k is fed back as input during the copy phase (98.5% of activation mass is on in_tok == k; never fires in the original or delimiter phase). Magnitude is strongly modulated by sequence length: strongest for L=3-4 (top examples are L=3 with k at recall position 1, ~0.9-1.0 of max), weaker for L=5, and essentially absent for L>=6 even when k is input during copy. Within short sequences it is concentrated on the last few copy steps (to_go <= 2). Does not fire on the original-phase k, on the first occurrence of a token, or on other copied tokens except a faint tail on a/b/f in very short sequences. Precision is incomplete mainly because many L=5 copy-phase k inputs stay inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: k, b, a, f; t=7: k; t=6: k, a, b, f) and the token being output (most: k, f, p, b, r, a; least: i, m, x, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
